newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian G-Bank says willing to look at cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Belgian G-Bank says willing to look at cooperation.

text.p: Generale Bank, Belgium's largest bank, reiterated on Thursday that it was willing to look at any proposal for cooperation with another bank, but said no talks were going on currently.

Chairman of the board Paul-Emmanuel Janssen also told the annual shareholders' meeting that if Generale Bank's indirect French parent Suez decided to reduce its stake in the bank, he was confident the bank would find other buyers.

"We will keep on growing, either internally or via acquisitions...Concerning growth via a merger...we take note of the fact that the market and the press talk about it all the time...." Janssen said in a speech to shareholders.

"It is obvious, and we have often said this before, that we are willing to investigate every cooperation (prospect) which can help us to play an important and autonomous role in the European banking world of tomorrow," he added.
"This investigation will not even be started if our board is not convinced from the outset that new shareholders will respect our autonomy and subscribe to our strategy," he said.
Janssen said that the bank still had a harmonious relationship with its parent company Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) and SGB's French parent Compagnie de Suez.

Last month Suez announced that it planned to merge with French utilities group Lyonnaise des Eaux, to form a world utility group which will focus on energy, water, waste management and communications.
The new group has made clear that finance does not belong to its core business and has indicated that it would be willing to reduce its stake in the Belgian bank.

"If the Suez/Lyonnaise group, with an eye on the development of its core business, in the future had to reduce its stake in the bank, the latter will in my opinion find other buyers which will...guarantee its autonomy and partake in its expansion," Janssens said.
He also reiterated that 1997 earnings will progress, as had been said two weeks ago at the publication of the annual report.
